title: Payload sparsifier & run-length microbatcher with kernel-cost evaluator for prefill/decode trimming
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Problem: At 99th-percentile load we see wasted token compute from padding-heavy micro-batches where a small fraction of long sequences force larger kernel selection and reduce packing density. This increases per-token cost and occasionally pushes decode latency over our SLOs when kernel switching occurs mid-decode.

Goal: Implement a microbatch shaping component (Payload Sparsifier + Run-Length Batcher) that dynamically trims and groups prefills/decodes by runtime-observed payload patterns and a kernel-cost evaluator. The component should: (1) reduce padded tokens by opportunistic run-length trimming and prefix concatenation where semantics allow, (2) choose kernel variants based on a cost model (latency vs compute) and predicted sequence-length distribution, (3) schedule prefill and decode phases to avoid expensive kernel swaps during time-critical decode windows, and (4) expose safe fallbacks for correctness and auditability.

Scope: Prototype in the inference runtime as an opt-in scheduling pass behind a feature flag. Focus on transformer models with sparse attention and KV cache prefill. Do not change model weights or tokenizer. Provide metrics to evaluate cost impact (tokens saved, kernel-switch frequency, p99 latency delta).

Non-goals: Full PL/SQL rollout automation, cross-region routing, and new quantization algorithms. Not targeting batched embeddings endpoints in this ticket (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime introduces a feature-flagged pass 'payload_sparsifier' that can trim run-length padding on prefills with a safety heuristic: only trim contiguous repeated pad tokens or repeated identical suffix tokens where decode semantics are preserved.

Kernel-cost evaluator reports expected latency and compute tradeoffs for candidate kernel variants given a seqlen histogram; runtime selects kernel variant per microbatch or per-decode-boundary to minimize p99 latency subject to a configurable compute budget.
End-to-end testbench demonstrating >=15% reduction in padded-tokens-per-batch on internal workload trace and no regressions in greedy decode outputs for validated prompts.
Telemetry: new dashboards show tokens_saved, kernel_switch_count, p50/p95/p99 latency by feature_flag:true vs false, and per-customer impact breakdown.

Documented fallback: when kernel selection would require a mid-decode swap that violates SLO, the scheduler preserves the cheaper decode ordering or applies an automatic prefill re-binning to avoid swap.
comments: 2025-02-21 - Initial spike: measured 18% median padding inefficiency and 2.3x kernel-cost multiplier on long-tail sequences in internal traffic logs. (Ethan)

2025-02-24 - Design review w/ runtime and kernels: agreed to build a micro-pass that operates at the request-cohort level, not per-request, to avoid per-request overhead. Trade-off: less optimal packing for edge cases but far lower scheduler overhead. (Aisha)
2025-02-26 - UX/Console: Need an admin toggle plus per-team opt-in. Added signal to debug traces for per-request padding decisions; linked to draft console change. (Marisol)

2025-03-01 - PR opened: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4821 implements pass skeleton + unit-tests for run-length detection. Perf harness added under infra/tests/payload_sparsifier. (PR author: A. Kapoor)

2025-03-03 - Kernel team feedback: kernel-cost estimator must consider warm vs cold kernel (cache priming) and GPU occupancy effects at different batch sizes. Action: add warmup penalty term to cost model. (Kernel team)

2025-03-05 - Integration test: end-to-end trace run shows 16% tokens_saved and kernel_switch_count halved for sample workload. Observed a small p50 latency increase (+3ms) for tiny batches — added a rule to disable sparsifier for batches under 4 requests. (Aisha)
To-do: add deterministic fallback path for requests with function-calling / tool-invocations to avoid accidental semantics changes.
implementation_notes: Architecture: add a scheduling pass after request-cohorting and before kernel-selection. The pass computes a seqlen histogram, applies run-length detection, and proposes microbatch transformations (trim, concat suffix, rebucket).

Kernel-cost model: inputs = {seqlen_histogram, batch_size, model_variant, gpu_type, warm_state_flag}. Output = expected_p50_latency_ms, expected_p99_latency_ms, normalized_compute_cost. Warm_state_flag indicates whether kernel is hot on device for given model variant.

Heuristics: (1) only trim contiguous suffix/pad sequences that are pure padding or guaranteed-idempotent suffix tokens, (2) avoid trimming when request has tool-call markers or non-deterministic tokens, (3) prefer concatenation over splitting when it reduces overall kernel count.

Safety: deterministic fallback path writes original request to trace log and replays unchanged if trimmed output deviates in unit tests. Maintain a 'safety seed' snapshot for any trimmed cohort for later audit.
Observability: emit per-cohort events: original_token_count, post_trim_token_count, chosen_kernel, estimated_cost_delta, actual_latency_ms. Correlate with model-eval promptsets to detect regressions.
Testing: add golden decode tests for 50 representative prompts, plus randomized fuzzing that checks equivalence for non-ambiguous trims. Run perf harness across A100, H100, and M60-equivalent clouds.

Rollout plan: feature-flag -> internal canary -> 10% tenant rollout -> measure 7-day regressions -> ramp. Abort criteria: >0.5% regression in generation accuracy on eval set OR p99 latency increase >5% for any tenant.
estimate_rationale: 8 points: design spike/coordination with kernel team (2), implement core pass + unit tests (3), perf harness and iterations (2), dashboards and rollout (1).
notes_for_reviewers: Pay attention to the warm-kernel penalty term in kernel-cost model; this is where most of the estimator tuning happens.
Validate that run-length trimming rules do not affect function-calling markers and that we log sufficient data for debug and audit.
Ensure the feature flag is granular enough to disable per-team without runtime restart.
